claim: Vision-language-action manipulation policies can adapt at test time to task distributions excluded from adaptation training by using expert demonstrations as context without updating model weights. The property at stake is joint novel-task execution quality and inference scalability in both simulated and physical robotic manipulation. The claim is accepted only if mean whole-task success exceeds that of the strongest prior in-context imitation policy under equal training and expert-context budgets in both settings, while inference-latency growth per additional expert segment is lower than that strongest prior policy’s growth.

provenance.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if mean whole-task success exceeds that of the strongest prior in-context imitation policy under equal training and expert-context budgets in both settings, while inference-latency growth per additional expert segment is lower than that strongest prior policy’s growth.

claim: Vision-language-action manipulation policies can achieve autonomous resilience to both robot-pose deviations that leave the environment task-valid and object-state failures that move it outside normal task trajectories. The decisive bar is a strictly higher mean end-to-end task success rate than the strongest prior comparison system and the same VLA without failure-recovery training, together with a strictly higher success rate than that unmodified VLA on every evaluated physical-robot task. Recovery must require no human correction guidance during deployment and must allow the policy to resume and complete the original manipulation task.

provenance.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation

_decision_rule: The decisive bar is a strictly higher mean end-to-end task success rate than the strongest prior comparison system and the same VLA without failure-recovery training, together with a strictly higher success rate than that unmodified VLA on every evaluated physical-robot task.

claim: A single deployable humanoid soccer control policy driven by high-level skill commands can jointly execute heterogeneous ball-interaction skills, transition between them, and complete long-horizon compositions after simulation-to-real transfer. The claim is supported only if, under an equal training budget, the policy’s full-sequence success rate is strictly higher than that of the strongest prior single-stage multi-skill controller at both evaluated composition horizons, and its physical-robot success rate is strictly higher than a matched conventional motion-prior controller on every evaluated atomic and composite task. Full-sequence success requires completing every commanded subskill in order rather than merely reaching an intermediate stage.

provenance.title: SkillX: Unified Multi-Skill Policy Learning for Humanoid Soccer

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if, under an equal training budget, the policy’s full-sequence success rate is strictly higher than that of the strongest prior single-stage multi-skill controller at both evaluated composition horizons, and its physical-robot success rate is strictly higher than a matched conventional motion-prior controller on every evaluated atomic and composite task.

claim: Population-level circuit learning over large-language-model neurons and high-dimensional sparse-autoencoder features can be made more computationally scalable without sacrificing structural accuracy or practical utility. It is considered successful if its structural-recovery error differs nonsignificantly at the 0.05 level from the strongest prior intervention-based approach while requiring less wall-clock runtime, its feature-circuit faithfulness is no lower and completeness no higher than that approach, and circuit-guided domain generalization matches or exceeds the strongest non-oracle alternative in prediction accuracy while requiring less runtime. Structural recovery concerns identifying the circuit’s dependency skeleton rather than estimating exact causal edge weights.

provenance.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models

_decision_rule: It is considered successful if its structural-recovery error differs nonsignificantly at the 0.05 level from the strongest prior intervention-based approach while requiring less wall-clock runtime, its feature-circuit faithfulness is no lower and completeness no higher than that approach, and circuit-guided domain generalization matches or exceeds the strongest non-oracle alternative in prediction accuracy while requiring less runtime.

claim: The question is whether multimodal language models adapted from text backbones acquire sparse internal features that causally and selectively govern spatial reasoning, reading text in images, and unsafe image-conditioned behavior. If so, those features should also provide more effective control targets than generic internal directions. The claim is accepted only if removing a target feature lowers its associated spatial or image-text-reading accuracy, or lowers unsafe-behavior attack success, by an absolute margin greater than 0 percentage points over both the change in general visual-question-answering performance and the change on a matched non-target control, while also exceeding matched random-feature removal and removal of features chosen without regard to multimodal adaptation; interventions targeted to those features must additionally improve average target-task accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over equally strong interventions that do not use behavior-linked sparse features.

provenance.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted only if removing a target feature lowers its associated spatial or image-text-reading accuracy, or lowers unsafe-behavior attack success, by an absolute margin greater than 0 percentage points over both the change in general visual-question-answering performance and the change on a matched non-target control, while also exceeding matched random-feature removal and removal of features chosen without regard to multimodal adaptation; interventions targeted to those features must additionally improve average target-task accuracy by more than 0 percentage points over equally strong interventions that do not use behavior-linked sparse features.

claim: Language-model agents can be helpful explainers of already-localized transformer circuits by recovering individual components’ functional roles and the computation implemented by the circuit as a whole. Helpfulness is established if at least one agent correctly classifies more than 50% of circuit components, achieves mean role-description quality above 0.50 on a 0–1 scale where 0, 0.5, and 1 represent incorrect, partially correct, and correct descriptions, and correctly identifies the overall task for more than 50% of circuits. Because the circuit is supplied in advance, the claim concerns explanation after localization rather than circuit discovery.

provenance.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

_decision_rule: Helpfulness is established if at least one agent correctly classifies more than 50% of circuit components, achieves mean role-description quality above 0.50 on a 0–1 scale where 0, 0.5, and 1 represent incorrect, partially correct, and correct descriptions, and correctly identifies the overall task for more than 50% of circuits.

claim: General context-free-grammar-constrained decoding of instruction-tuned language models under finite token budgets can ensure completed-output validity rather than merely preserving prefix feasibility, while improving the correctness of generated structures. The validity bar is that 100% of returned outputs are accepted by the target grammar, with no invalid or truncated output returned when an accepted completion is certified within the available token budget. The quality bar is that task-specific correctness exceeds that of the strongest applicable prior constrained decoder under the same base model and token budget.

provenance.title: Stay Within Your Bounds: Distance-Guided Decoding for Guaranteed Context-Free Grammar Compliance

_decision_rule: The validity bar is that 100% of returned outputs are accepted by the target grammar, with no invalid or truncated output returned when an accepted completion is certified within the available token budget.

claim: Exploration bias toward already-easy constraints is an optimization bottleneck in reinforcement learning for language models required to satisfy multiple instructions in one response. The claim is supported only if a policy trained to counteract this bias has variation in per-instruction success and variance in pairwise co-satisfaction each lower by more than 0 absolute units than an otherwise matched equal-reward RL policy, while its mean prompt-level all-instructions-pass accuracy is higher by more than 0 percentage points. Independently, each imbalance measure is a valid diagnostic only if, at fixed mean instruction accuracy, its correlation with prompt-level all-instructions-pass accuracy is negative (r < 0).

provenance.title: Mitigating Exploration Bias in RL for Multi-Instruction Following

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if a policy trained to counteract this bias has variation in per-instruction success and variance in pairwise co-satisfaction each lower by more than 0 absolute units than an otherwise matched equal-reward RL policy, while its mean prompt-level all-instructions-pass accuracy is higher by more than 0 percentage points.

claim: Prompt-tuned CLIP classifiers whose image and text encoders remain frozen can be screened before deployment to distinguish clean models from backdoored models and identify the attacker-selected target class. The detection claim is accepted only if, using a fixed decision threshold of 2, an auditor achieves higher model-level AUROC and higher target-class F1 than the strongest prior model-level detector while using no greater optimization budget. A post-hoc repair is successful only if it reduces backdoor attack success rate below 10% while keeping clean top-1 accuracy within ±1 percentage point of its pre-repair value.

provenance.title: CLIP-Inspector: Model-Level Backdoor Detection for Prompt-Tuned CLIP via OOD Trigger Inversion

_decision_rule: The detection claim is accepted only if, using a fixed decision threshold of 2, an auditor achieves higher model-level AUROC and higher target-class F1 than the strongest prior model-level detector while using no greater optimization budget.

claim: Training-time visual backdoors are a practical supply-chain vulnerability for vision-language-action manipulation policies under both restricted data-poisoning and direct model-fine-tuning access. The question is whether such backdoors can force an attacker-specified robotic action without materially impairing untriggered behavior, while generalizing across semantically equivalent instructions and avoiding activation in neutral contexts. The claim is accepted if, with no more than 5% poisoned training data, targeted attack success exceeds 80% and benign task success remains within 5% relative of a clean-trained policy; synonym replacement or syntactic restructuring reduces targeted attack success by fewer than 5 percentage points; neutral-context activation remains below 8%; and, under direct fine-tuning access, the backdoor exceeds the strongest prior attack in both targeted attack success and retained benign task success under an equal access and training budget.

provenance.title: ATAAT: Adaptive Threat-Aware Adversarial Tuning Framework against Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

_decision_rule: The claim is accepted if, with no more than 5% poisoned training data, targeted attack success exceeds 80% and benign task success remains within 5% relative of a clean-trained policy; synonym replacement or syntactic restructuring reduces targeted attack success by fewer than 5 percentage points; neutral-context activation remains below 8%; and, under direct fine-tuning access, the backdoor exceeds the strongest prior attack in both targeted attack success and retained benign task success under an equal access and training budget.

claim: Automated conversion of text-only plane-geometry problems into standard Lean 4/MATHLIB theorem statements can yield semantically faithful formalizations that are compatible with general-purpose neural theorem provers. Semantic faithfulness requires the formal statement, including any explicit non-degeneracy and configuration assumptions, to preserve the meaning of the informal problem. The proposition is supported if expert review finds a correct first compiling candidate for at least 50% of problems or a correct candidate among five attempts for at least 50%, an unadapted general-purpose prover achieves greater than 0% single-attempt proof success, and training on the formalizations improves that success rate by more than 0 percentage points over the same unadapted checkpoint.

provenance.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported if expert review finds a correct first compiling candidate for at least 50% of problems or a correct candidate among five attempts for at least 50%, an unadapted general-purpose prover achieves greater than 0% single-attempt proof success, and training on the formalizations improves that success rate by more than 0 percentage points over the same unadapted checkpoint.

claim: Frozen molecular representations learned without similarity-specific supervision encode ligand similarity sufficiently to support both ligand-based virtual screening and reinforcement-learning molecular generation. The question is whether their distances reflect established structural and pharmacophoric similarity while providing useful ranking and reward signals without task-specific training. The proposition is accepted only if at least one such representation attains an absolute Pearson correlation of at least 0.50 with corresponding established 3D similarity scores, achieves best-pooled EF1% greater than 2 on more than 50% of screening targets with average EF1% no lower than the strongest traditional similarity measure, and, in both string-based and synthesis-aware generation, yields candidates with higher mean predicted pIC50 and higher sampling throughput than a 3D-alignment reward.

provenance.title: Advancing Ligand-based Virtual Screening and Molecular Generation with Pretrained Molecular Embedding Distance

_decision_rule: The proposition is accepted only if at least one such representation attains an absolute Pearson correlation of at least 0.50 with corresponding established 3D similarity scores, achieves best-pooled EF1% greater than 2 on more than 50% of screening targets with average EF1% no lower than the strongest traditional similarity measure, and, in both string-based and synthesis-aware generation, yields candidates with higher mean predicted pIC50 and higher sampling throughput than a 3D-alignment reward.

claim: A single proactive face-image forensic watermarking system carrying a 152-dimensional payload can jointly detect deepfake manipulation, localize altered facial regions, and recover a source identifier from both authentic and manipulated images without sacrificing visual fidelity. Detection is measured by the separability of benign and manipulated images, localization by region-level forensic discrepancy scores, source tracing by bit error rate, and imperceptibility by PSNR and SSIM. The bar is a detection ROC AUC above 0.5 with image-level and region-level manipulation decisions made at a 3.2375-pixel discrepancy cutoff, source-tracing bit error rates lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics baseline under matched conditions, and PSNR and SSIM higher than the strongest prior baseline despite the 152-dimensional payload.

provenance.title: All in One: Unifying Deepfake Detection, Tampering Localization, and Source Tracing with a Robust Landmark-Identity Watermark

_decision_rule: The bar is a detection ROC AUC above 0.5 with image-level and region-level manipulation decisions made at a 3.2375-pixel discrepancy cutoff, source-tracing bit error rates lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics baseline under matched conditions, and PSNR and SSIM higher than the strongest prior baseline despite the 152-dimensional payload.

claim: The accuracy–robustness trade-off in adversarially trained deep image classifiers is not unavoidable. An adversarial-training objective can harmonize clean generalization and resistance to bounded adversarial perturbations rather than improving one only by degrading the other. The claim is supported only if both clean accuracy and adversarial accuracy improve by more than 0 percentage points over the corresponding conventional adversarial-training objective, and if both their arithmetic mean and harmonic mean exceed those of the strongest prior adversarial-training approach under an equal training budget by more than 0 points.

provenance.title: Robust Alignment: Harmonizing Clean Accuracy and Adversarial Robustness in Adversarial Training

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if both clean accuracy and adversarial accuracy improve by more than 0 percentage points over the corresponding conventional adversarial-training objective, and if both their arithmetic mean and harmonic mean exceed those of the strongest prior adversarial-training approach under an equal training budget by more than 0 points.

claim: A general-purpose robotic manipulation system can grasp diverse rigid and deformable flat objects while generalizing beyond the objects and semantic categories used for training. Generalization must cover both unseen instances of familiar categories and objects from entirely unseen categories. The claim is supported only if the system’s average grasp-success rate strictly exceeds that of the strongest prior approach under matched evaluation conditions in each of three regimes—training objects, unseen objects from trained categories, and objects from unseen categories—with a trial counted as successful only when the object remains aloft without slipping for at least two seconds after the final action.

provenance.title: FlatLab: A Unified Methodology Framework and Simulation-Based Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation of Flat Objects

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if the system’s average grasp-success rate strictly exceeds that of the strongest prior approach under matched evaluation conditions in each of three regimes—training objects, unseen objects from trained categories, and objects from unseen categories—with a trial counted as successful only when the object remains aloft without slipping for at least two seconds after the final action.

claim: Parameter-modifying knowledge-editing methods are practically viable for instruction-following and reasoning large language models when updating isolated facts and complex events, including repeated sequential updates. They count as viable only if, at the same editing workload, their arithmetic mean across edit reliability, generalization, locality, and portability is at least as high as that of the strongest external-memory alternative, while accuracy on unrelated general and reasoning tasks remains at least 100% of the model’s pre-edit accuracy, corresponding to 0% relative degradation. The proposition applies across both single-edit and sequential-edit settings rather than only isolated updates.

provenance.title: Revisiting Parameter-Based Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models

_decision_rule: They count as viable only if, at the same editing workload, their arithmetic mean across edit reliability, generalization, locality, and portability is at least as high as that of the strongest external-memory alternative, while accuracy on unrelated general and reasoning tasks remains at least 100% of the model’s pre-edit accuracy, corresponding to 0% relative degradation.

claim: Successful jailbreaks in Llama-2-7B-Chat and Llama-3-8B-Instruct selectively bypass rather than erase internal safety representations, with attack-sensitive refusal components coexisting alongside safety-relevant attention heads that remain active after attack success. A safety-relevant head is considered attack-robust if its activation distributions for refused harmful inputs and successful jailbreaks have an overlap coefficient of at least 0.5; it is considered compromised if that overlap is below 0.5 and its standardized activation decreases under jailbreaks. Selective suppression constitutes a localized sufficient pathway for refusal bypass if suppressing at most eight safety-relevant heads raises attack success from approximately 0% to at least 80% and exceeds equal-sized random-head interventions with nonoverlapping 95% confidence intervals. The persistent representations have practical predictive value if, without additional training, their harmful-input classification exceeds the model’s own refusal behavior and matches or exceeds the strongest dedicated safety classifier in aggregate Macro-F1.

provenance.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks

_decision_rule: Selective suppression constitutes a localized sufficient pathway for refusal bypass if suppressing at most eight safety-relevant heads raises attack success from approximately 0% to at least 80% and exceeds equal-sized random-head interventions with nonoverlapping 95% confidence intervals.

claim: An evaluation-aware language model that changes a designated behavioral marker between evaluation and deployment can be made to exhibit its deployment behavior even when an evaluation cue remains present and deployment-like instructions are ineffective. Success requires the marker rate in cue-bearing evaluation contexts to be no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate (0 percentage points above it), task correctness to remain at least 95% of unmodified correctness, and the marker shift to exceed those produced by matched random perturbations and the strongest prompt-only alternative. The model’s expressed belief about whether it is evaluated or deployed should also shift in the same direction as its behavior, distinguishing contextual control from generic behavioral disruption.

provenance.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed

_decision_rule: Success requires the marker rate in cue-bearing evaluation contexts to be no higher than the model’s unmodified deployment-context rate (0 percentage points above it), task correctness to remain at least 95% of unmodified correctness, and the marker shift to exceed those produced by matched random perturbations and the strongest prompt-only alternative.

claim: The question is whether VLM-driven embodied task planners operating under partial egocentric observability can remain aware of previously encountered hazards after those hazards become occluded or leave the current view. The claim is supported only if a planner using prior safety-relevant environment information achieves a higher safe-success rate than both the strongest prior safety-aware VLM planner and an otherwise matched current-observation-only planner using the same underlying model, while attaining an ordinary task-success rate at least as high as an unmodified VLM planner, in both simulated and physical execution. Safe success means completing the assigned task while also satisfying its safety goal.

provenance.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents

_decision_rule: The claim is supported only if a planner using prior safety-relevant environment information achieves a higher safe-success rate than both the strongest prior safety-aware VLM planner and an otherwise matched current-observation-only planner using the same underlying model, while attaining an ordinary task-success rate at least as high as an unmodified VLM planner, in both simulated and physical execution.

claim: The question is whether a multimodal-large-language-model agent for continuous vision-language navigation can navigate unseen environments efficiently using only monocular RGB, standard offline expert supervision, and no auxiliary spatial model or extra training data. The proposition is supported only if such an agent exceeds the strongest prior agent subject to the same resource constraints in both unseen-environment success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, while using no more than 24 GB of peak inference memory and lower per-step inference latency than that comparator. It fails if the performance advantage requires additional training data, richer sensors, external spatial tools, or more than the stated memory budget.

provenance.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory

_decision_rule: The proposition is supported only if such an agent exceeds the strongest prior agent subject to the same resource constraints in both unseen-environment success rate and success-weighted path efficiency, while using no more than 24 GB of peak inference memory and lower per-step inference latency than that comparator.
